clue.text: Many poodles without a lead

definitions.note: the answer is a noun meaning lots; read as 'many' it stands in for a large quantity

indicators.note: a lead is what goes in front, so the word loses its opening letter; the surface means dogs off the leash

parts.note: taken as written: the dogs themselves supply the letters

explanation.surface: A crowd of poodles running about off the leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a lead' reads as dogs let off the leash, but it asks for the first letter of poodles to go.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an informal word for a great abundance, a synonym of lots.

clue.text: Former writing expert

parts.note: former times are old times
a person's hand is their handwriting

explanation.surface: Someone who used to be a skilled penman.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is an idiom for a veteran with long experience, a seasoned expert.

clue.text: Top journalist turned up in storehouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
ED is short for editor, the top journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A senior reporter appears at a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like arriving, but it reverses the letters of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a place where goods are stored, a warehouse.

clue.text: Comfortable seat for undemanding director

parts.note: an easy task is undemanding
the chair is the person directing a meeting or board

explanation.surface: A cosy armchair reserved for a boss who asks little of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a soft upholstered armchair, built for comfort.

clue.text: Toiler needs half a plum and more rum

indicators.note: take only half a word, here its first two letters

parts.note: its first half is PL
rum means odd, so more rum is odder

explanation.surface: A worker who wants half a plum and another tot of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is the old British adjective meaning strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A plodder works slowly and steadily, a toiler who gets there by sheer effort.

clue.text: Describe how Raymond has taken to strong wine

indicators.note: one piece attaches itself after the other, as Ray takes to the bottle

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
Ray is the short form of the name

explanation.surface: An account of how a man called Raymond got into the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent in words or pictures.

clue.text: Drops no longer moist

indicators.note: the word is no longer in its original form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Drops of water have dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' seems to belong with moist as water droplets, but it is the verb meaning leaves out.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, as when a team leaves out or drops a player.

clue.text: Opposing Sid, going up and down with damaged net

parts.note: the name Sid read upwards then downwards in a down entry, giving it backwards and then forwards

indicators.note: a damaged net is broken out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sid, in opposition, is bobbing about beside a broken net.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident is someone who dissents, so the word works adjectivally for disagreeing with authority.

clue.text: Playboy lifts me up in new version of old film

indicators.note: the playboy holds up the other piece inside himself, so it is enclosed

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man about town

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A playboy hoists the narrator in a fresh take on a classic movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A remake is a new production of a film made before, retelling the same story.

clue.text: He keeps going, but does he?

definitions.meaning: one with stamina who lasts the course
the word also suggests one who stays put, the opposite of keeping going

explanation.walkthrough: The answer means someone with staying power, yet to stay is to stop, so the clue asks whether he really keeps moving.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a horse or runner with endurance, able to last a long race.

clue.text: Ted is poor, no longer a bank customer

indicators.note: the words are no longer as they stood, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the last of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ted has gone broke and so has closed his account.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies Ted has stopped banking; in fact 'poor' is fodder and 'no longer' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A depositor is someone who places money in an account, a bank's client.

clue.text: I'm affected with sun briefly

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complaining of sunstroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in short, to summarise, so it stands for concisely.

clue.text: Half anticipate a trick

indicators.note: only half of the ten-letter word is kept, so its second half is dropped

parts.note: taken as written; its first five letters are kept

explanation.surface: Half-expect someone to play a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or grotesque caper, a prank.

clue.text: Get the measure of removing Darcy's kit

indicators.note: removing means moving the letters elsewhere, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Size up Mr Darcy by taking his clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: Darcy is the hero of Pride and Prejudice; 'removing' looks like undressing but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard used for comparison, a gauge.

clue.text: Endless desire to bottle up father's gloom

indicators.note: to bottle up is to hold inside, so one piece contains the other
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before its final letter goes
Pa is an informal word for father; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Bottling up a longing for one's father leads to sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a deep gloom.

clue.text: Sell amber shaped as something trivial

indicators.note: shaped means formed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Trading amber after carving it into some little trinket.
explanation.walkthrough: Small beer is a British idiom, originally weak beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is an idiom for something of little importance, a trifle.

clue.text: One gets dry mixture over there

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is handed a dry blend of something across the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned word for at a distance, in that place.

clue.text: Still sees lions running around

definitions.note: an adjective here, meaning silent, not the adverb

indicators.note: the letters run around into a new order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A quiet watcher sees lions moving about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb opening the sentence, but it is the adjective meaning quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Still can mean silent or hushed, making no sound.

clue.text: Pretty one may speak straight from the shoulder

definitions.meaning: Pretty Polly is the stock phrase taught to talking birds
an idiom for frank speech, but literally from a pirate's shoulder where the bird perches

explanation.walkthrough: Speaking straight from the shoulder means talking bluntly, but a pirate's talking bird literally speaks from his shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a talking bird, classically perched on a pirate's shoulder.

clue.text: Receipts found in attractive square

parts.note: taking in its sense of captivating or charming
S is a recognised abbreviation for square, as in street names

explanation.surface: Money discovered in a pretty town square.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the money a business brings in, its revenue.

clue.text: What to call male stranger hiding hole in damper

indicators.note: the term of address hides the other piece inside it

parts.note: the polite form of address for a man whose name you don't know
O looks like a hole

explanation.surface: A puzzle over how to address an unknown man concealed in something wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Moister is the comparative of moist, meaning wetter.

clue.text: French woman finds me sitting astride a wall

indicators.note: the outer word sits astride, with one letter on either side of the inner piece

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a dam is a wall holding back water

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman discovers the speaker perched on top of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, used as a word for a Frenchwoman.

clue.text: Particular honour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a detail or point
second meaning: to esteem or revere

explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular honour' reads as a special award; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an aspect or detail and high regard or esteem.

clue.text: Thick hair? Not this child!

parts.note: the alternative to this is that

explanation.surface: A shock of hair, but not on this particular youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is a jocular word for a dense mop of hair, likened to a straw roof.

clue.text: Unplanned, like a bun in the oven?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ill-conceived, not thought through

definitions.text: like a bun in the oven?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: a bun partly cooked is literally half done

explanation.walkthrough: 'A bun in the oven' is slang for a pregnancy, which nudges 'Unplanned' toward babies; the answer is the idiom for a poorly thought-out scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a scheme poorly thought out, and literally means undercooked.

clue.text: Old boy turns up with award for ice cream

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: OB, a former pupil of a school
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: A former pupil arrives with his medal to claim a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: An MBE is a British honour given in the monarch's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a frozen dessert of ice cream moulded in a dome.

clue.text: Leaves not starting to reveal part of the roof

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Leaves lying on a roof, with something unable to start.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaves are the edges of a roof that overhang the walls.

clue.text: Music maker in "Twelfth Night"

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the stringed instrument, a little larger than a violin
second meaning: the heroine of Shakespeare's comedy, who disguises herself as a boy

explanation.walkthrough: Twelfth Night opens with 'If music be the food of love', which makes the two halves read as one idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bowed string instrument and Shakespeare's shipwrecked heroine.

clue.text: A quantity of heat, which in a word is hot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British unit of heat used for gas bills

definitions.text: which in a word is hot
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Greek-derived element meaning heat, found inside words like thermometer

explanation.walkthrough: The second half means 'the part of a word that signals heat', as in thermal or thermostat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a unit of 100,000 British thermal units and the word-forming element meaning warmth.

clue.text: First person in crowd to go to United

indicators.note: the first piece goes next to the second, which follows it

parts.note: a number of people is a crowd of them
united means made one

explanation.surface: The first fan in the crowd heads off to watch Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club but means joined into a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for oneself, putting one's own interests first.

clue.text: Large wasps in bag swallowed by tailless horse

indicators.note: the outer piece swallows the inner one, so it goes inside
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes
to net is to bag or catch

explanation.surface: A horse with a docked tail gulps down a sack of giant wasps.
explanation.definitionFit: Hornets are the largest kind of wasp, with a painful sting.

clue.text: Obliquely, like a social worker standing behind a learner

indicators.note: one piece stands after another in the answer

parts.note: as in its sense of in the manner of
L is the learner plate on a car
the ant is a social insect, and the worker ant does the colony's labour

explanation.surface: Someone stands crookedly, like a social worker waiting behind a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer, but it is an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at a slant, on a diagonal.
